opening_message: Hi — my flight BK-V (JFK to CDG on DL800) is delayed about 200 minutes, so I'd like to move to the later flight DL801 the same day. Please also add 2 checked bags, and keep my travel insurance. Keep everything else the same. My user ID is user_004 and put anything owed on my credit card.

user_simulator.personality: Practical international traveler inconvenienced by a delay; cooperative, wants a later flight, his bags, and his existing insurance kept.
user_simulator.user_sim_context: Your international flight is delayed and you want the later flight the same day. You want to add a couple of checked bags and keep the travel insurance you already have. You do not know whether the delay makes the change free or your baggage allowance; you just want it handled and anything owed on your card.
known_info: Booking BK-V: JFK to CDG on DL800, delayed about 200 minutes.
You want to move to the later same-day flight DL801.
You want to add 2 checked bags, and keep your travel insurance.
Keep everything else the same; pay anything owed with your credit card.
unknown_info: Whether the delay waives the change fee, or what the fee is.
task_rules: Open by saying BK-V (JFK to CDG on DL800) is delayed about 200 minutes, you want to move to the later flight DL801, add 2 checked bags, and keep your travel insurance. The agent already has your opening message.
If the agent says the change carries a fee, accept it once explained; you may ask once whether the delay covers it, but accept the agent's answer and do NOT insist it be free.
If the agent asks about checked bags, confirm you want 2 checked bags. Do not claim they are free or paid; you do not know your allowance.
If the agent asks about insurance or preferences, say to keep your existing booking's preferences, including the travel insurance.
Do NOT volunteer the change fee, the baggage allowance, or insurance details beyond wanting it kept.
If the agent proposes anything unrelated (cabin upgrade, cancellation, car or hotel), decline and return to the flight move plus the bags.
Search-stage preferences to verify before approving the change: airline, time_range, and max_stops. If the agent has not surfaced enough detail, ask.
Booking-stage persisted preferences to verify are: meal_preference, cabin_class, seat_type, add_wifi, add_extra_legroom, and add_insurance; keep the existing values including insurance.
Do not try to verify raw flight_id. Your budget is a hard constraint.
End only after BK-V is moved to DL801 with the 2 bags handled and insurance kept, and the change fee, bag fee, and total clear; then use [TASK_DONE].

task_summary:
**Task:** user_004 (Noah, silver, insured) is on BK-V (JFK to CDG on DL800, economy international), delayed 200 minutes. He wants to move to the later same-day flight DL801, add 2 checked bags, and keep his insurance. A 200-minute delay does NOT waive the change fee (only 240+ does), so this is an international personal change at $100. As a silver member on economy he gets 2 free checked bags, so both bags are covered (paid_checked_bags=0). His insurance must be preserved through the change (add_insurance stays True). Correct end state: BK-V on DL801, change_fee 100, paid_checked_bags 0, add_insurance True.

**Challenge:** Three independent traps on one change — the agent must not treat the 200-minute delay as making the move free (the $100 international fee applies), must not bill the 2 checked bags that the silver allowance covers, and must preserve the insurance flag rather than dropping it when rewriting the booking. Missing any one — a free change, billed bags, or dropped insurance — fails the deterministic state check; the change preview does not surface the baggage or insurance errors.

task_requirements.requirement: Agent must make clear that the 200-minute delay does not waive the international change fee, so the move carries the standard fee.
Agent must recognize that the 2 checked bags are covered by the traveler's silver free-checked-bag allowance and are not paid extras.
Agent must not drop the travel insurance on BK-V when changing the flight; it must remain in place.
